newsitem.title: UK: UK retailers welcome prudent budget - BRC.
newsitem.headline: UK retailers welcome prudent budget - BRC.

text.p: Britain's retailers welcomed a modest income tax cut within an overall prudent budget package, the British Retail Consortium said on Tuesday.

"This is a well-judged budget," said Andrew Higginson, chairman of the BRC's economic affairs committee. "The Chancellor has resisted the pressure for a big pre-election giveaway but has provided reassurance for consumers that personal taxes will remain on a downward track."
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke cut the basic rate of income tax by one penny to 23 percent and widened the bands of the 20 percent starting rate and tax-free allowance.
Overall, he said tax cuts worth two billion pounds were matched by planned spending cuts of the same amount.

Higginson said the income tax cut was welcome for two reasons. "It should help maintain the current momentum in retail sales which is being achieved without price inflation. And...it focuses on the lower income levels, helping to tackle certain anomalies that reduce the incentives to work."
